input.prompt: An authentic Srikalahasti kalamkari hand-painted cotton textile panel, a sibling of the reference image: reproduce its craft exactly (the same lotus drawing with ecru petals outlined in iron-black and filled with tiny madder-red dots, the same dot-filled curling branches, cross-hatched paisley leaves, olive-green leaves, visible hand-woven cotton weave, slight wobble and dye bleed) and its lotus-and-vine border, but with a NEW composition. It must look like a real hand-painted cloth photographed flat, NOT a clean digital vector illustration. The cloth fills the entire frame edge to edge. The ground of the panel is undyed ecru cotton. COMPOSITION, exactly two people: a young Telugu man and a young Telugu woman sit cross-legged on a madder-red dotted mat in the lower half, facing each other in side profile, both mid-conversation with one hand raised palm-up in an open, expressive talking gesture. Their skin is left as undyed ecru cotton outlined in black, as in classical kalamkari. The man (left) has short black hair, a neat short black beard, and spectacles: a clearly drawn round black-rimmed lens circle around his almond eye with a thin black arm running back to his ear. He wears a kurta of indigo with white dots. The woman (right) has long black hair in a single braid down her back, and wears a madder-red saree with a turmeric-yellow border and fine dot pattern. Classical kalamkari figure drawing: large almond eyes, gentle smiles, stylised hands with five slender fingers, flowing patterned drapery. THE KEY MOTIF: from each of their raised open palms a slender dot-filled vine with small olive leaves rises upward (the vines do not touch their faces); the two vines curve toward each other, twist around each other twice in the open ecru space between and above their heads, and join into ONE single large blooming lotus (ecru petals with madder-red dots, like the reference) that floats directly above and between their heads, the focal point of the panel. A single blossoming tree grows at the far left edge behind the man, its dot-filled trunk at the side, its curling branches arching across the top of the panel like a canopy of dotted lotus blossoms, cross-hatched paisley leaves and buds. On one branch at the top centre, directly above the central lotus, exactly two green parrots with indigo wings perch close together facing each other beak to beak, mirroring the couple below. Only two birds in the whole panel. A narrow band of small flowering plants on the ground beneath the mat. A dense ornamental border runs around all four edges: a lotus-and-vine scroll on madder red between two thin dotted bands, identical in style to the reference. Palette strictly: deep madder red, brick red, indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, olive green from indigo over yellow, and undyed ecru cotton; no bright pink. Completely flat, no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. The vines are purely botanical. No text, no letters, no script, no writing, no numbers, no speech bubbles, no lamps, no diyas, no candles, no fire, no flames. Exactly two human figures and exactly two birds.
